lines.en: A door with a picture of two little baby angels blushing.
Gabriel's lips twitched as she looked at the nameplate on the door: [Uriel☆].
[Hey.]
She knocked, but there was no answer.
Then, once more.
[Hey, Uriel!]
When she pounded harder, a groan came from beyond the door.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ tells you to get lost.]
Gabriel furrowed her brow at the resounding indirect message.
[You think I wanted to come here? I'm only here because of my assignment.]
Gabriel huffed as though merely talking about it was enough to drive her mad with irritation.
Already her second day on the unreasonable assignment Metatron had ordered her to take.
She had planned to slack off while pretending to do the bare minimum, but Metatron had preempted her.
─Gabriel, please begin by receiving a handover from Uriel. And Jophiel, please keep an eye on Gabriel to make sure she does not laze about.
─Leave it to me.
Of all people, she had to be teamed up with that stickler Jophiel.
She would have been better off on a team with Uriel.
[You've got observation records on the Demon King of Salvation, right? I'm here to pick them up. Hurry up and open the door!]
A rustling sound came from beyond the door.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ asks if you are really her replacement.]
[Yeah, you ■wit.]
Once again, an indirect message thundered out.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ says, ‘■■■■’.]
[If you're going to swear at me, why don't you come out and do it to my face?]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ asks if you are her only replacement.]
[Me and Jophiel.]
A deep sigh came from beyond the door.
A moment later, long, slender fingertips poked out through the barely opened door.
On closer inspection, there was something held between those pale fingers. Gabriel clicked her tongue when she realized what it was.
[······A USB drive? Who uses these anymore? Aren't these just for humans?]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ warns you to stop complaining and take it.]
As Gabriel took the USB drive, Uriel added one more thing.
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ says to keep it a secret from the Red Cosmos.]
[From Jophiel? Why?]
Uriel gave no answer, merely slamming the door shut.

All that came instead was intermittent sniffling. Gabriel, who had been about to snap something back, pursed her lips. They didn't usually get along, but seeing Uriel, the ‘Demon Hunter’, in such a state still bothered her.
[Hey, stop moping. Your confinement will be over before you know it. It's only three years······.]
[The constellation ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ shouts at you to get lost!]
[Crazy ■ gives me sh■ even when I try to comfort her.]
A little later, Gabriel returned to her room with the files and opened the USB drive.
And.
[······What kind of assignment were you even doing?]
Even as she muttered those words, Gabriel couldn't tear her eyes away from the video playing on the screen.
[The constellation ‘Lily Blooming in Aquarius’ is curious about you.]
[The constellation ‘Lily Blooming in Aquarius’ enjoys watching you.]
Jung Heewon frowned at the voice coming from thin air.
Now that Uriel was gone, an even stranger constellation had latched on to her.
That wasn't the only thing bothering her.
Jung Heewon gazed at Kim Dokja, who was roaming about in the distance.
“······Why hasn't he said anything to me?”
“Said what?”
She turned with a start to find Lee Jihye right beside her again.
“Nothing.”
“Why? What is it?”
“I said it's nothing.”
“Unnie, are you thinking of joining <Kim Dokja’s Company>?”
Jung Heewon, who had been gulping down a drink she bought at a street stall, spluttered and coughed.
“Wh-what? No! The name's weird, too. I'd be embarrassed to tell anyone I joined a place like that!”
“I'm looking forward to it. The company name is pretty lame, but it feels like getting a taste of working life, so I'm excited. Think we'll get paid, too?”
“You'll change your mind once you find out what working life is actually like.”
Lee Jihye pouted.
“Anyway, I'm waiting for a chance to join, too. Master's there, after all.”
“······Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi already joined?”
“Dokja-ajusshi said so, remember? ‘This is Yoo Joonghyuk's and my nebula!’”
Of course, he had never said anything of the sort, but Jung Heewon reflexively looked up into the air. The indirect message she expected never came. Somehow, something felt missing.
[The constellation ‘Lily Blooming in Aquarius’ dislikes incarnation ‘Lee Jihye’s’ humor.]
Jung Heewon shook her head and watched Kim Dokja bustling around the square.
For the past few days, he had been so busy she barely saw him, but she had no idea what he was working so hard at.
As Jung Heewon wandered around, feeling rather hurt, she caught sight of Yoo Sangah. She waved cheerfully at Yoo Sangah, who sat on a bench staring blankly into space.
“Sangah-ssi! Have you joined Dokja-ssi's nebula, by any chance?”
Noticing Jung Heewon, Yoo Sangah looked up with a start.
What had this woman been thinking about for the past few days to look so utterly distracted······?
“My circumstances are a little······.”
“Oh, right. It would be a bit difficult for you, Sangah-ssi.”

Yoo Sangah was an incarnation of the nebula <Olympus>. As a special case supported by an entire nebula, she would have trouble joining Kim Dokja's. It was obvious what would happen if, after having already accepted all that support, she chose another nebula now.
“We've agreed on an alliance instead. Through me, a few constellations have agreed to establish friendly relations with Dokja-ssi······.
“······Didn't all the constellations in <Olympus> hate Dokja-ssi?”
“Not all of them. Have you joined the nebula, Heewon-ssi?”
“I'm going to think about it.”
Jung Heewon smacked her lips and looked back toward the square.
“Actually, I'm not sure I'll join. There's the matter of my sponsor, too······.”
As Jung Heewon made excuses, her pride needlessly wounded, Yoo Sangah smiled gently.
“It would be a great help to Dokja-ssi if you joined the nebula, Heewon-ssi.”
“I'd like to help if I can.”
Fortunately or unfortunately, she didn't seem to be the only one in such a complicated position.

Farther away, in the middle of the square, Lee Hyunsung sat like a lumbering big dog. Beside him, Shin Yoosung and Lee Gilyoung crouched like kittens, all three watching Kim Dokja. More precisely, they were trailing after him whenever he moved.
It seemed obvious what they were waiting for. Kim Dokja had to be pretty heartless to keep ignoring them like that.
“······Looks like he hasn't said anything to them yet, either.”
Jung Heewon nodded at Lee Jihye's words.
“He'll tell us when the time comes. He's got a stubborn streak.”
Well, what did it matter?
Peace had finally come to the group for once, and Kim Dokja would need time to think about various things, too.
If all she had to do was wait like this, with nothing happening, she could wait forever.
[The constellation ‘Lily Blooming in Aquarius’ watches you fondly.]
[The constellation ‘Commander of the Red Cosmos’ is wary of the ‘Demon King of Salvation’.]
······With these strange angels around, she wouldn't be bored for a while, either.
Carelessly, Jung Heewon let herself relax.
And
it began, without warning.
“Seriously? There's no way at all to contact them, ajumma?”
“The channels leading to the Demon Realm are being blocked. As though a powerful barrier has appeared······.”
At Lee Sookyung's words, Han Sooyoung's expression grew increasingly bleak.

She had even been calling for a dokkaebi for some time, but not a single one had responded. Han Sooyoung stared blankly down at the bowl of water used for [Good or Bad Luck, Disaster or Happiness Fortune].
凶凶凶凶凶凶凶凶凶凶······.
She couldn't even count how many characters for ill fortune (凶) had appeared.
“What the hell is about to happen······?”

When the omen had been great ill fortune, Kim Dokja had been forced to face none other than one of the <Lokapala> of <Vedas>. But this many ill omens······ It was beyond great ill fortune. It deserved to be called a deluge of ill fortune (氾凶).
Bzzzzzt.
The surface of the water trembled, and faint sparks began to fly.
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ jerks his head up.]
“Flame Dragon?”
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ looks toward the 73rd Demon Realm.]
“Do you know something?”
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ lets out a threatening roar.]
Her heavily bandaged arm throbbed, and sparks flew from her body, which had synchronized with the Black Flame Dragon.
“Ugh, you jerk!”
The Black Flame Dragon's emotions flowed straight into her. No matter what opponent he had encountered before, he had never gone wild like this.
[The constellation ‘Expert at Sitting on the Fence’ bites their lips, which have turned blue.]
[The constellation ‘Guam Divine Doctor’ drops his acupuncture needles.]
[The constellation ‘Great King Heoncheon Hongdo Gyeongmun Wimu’ quietly sets down his sword.]
[The constellation ‘First Spiritualist of Joseon’ conceals his presence.]
The constellations of the Korean Peninsula were extinguishing their light.
Like prey hiding from a predator.
Her bandaged arm kept stinging.

Brushing aside Lee Sookyung's attempts to stop her, Han Sooyoung finally unwound the bandages. The Black Flame Dragon tattoo beneath them was glowing. With a crackle of sparks, Han Sooyoung's right arm wrote pitch-black letters in the air.
―The calamity of the stars is coming.
“The calamity of the stars? What's that?”

A situation so urgent that even the arrogant ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ had to communicate his wishes directly. She could feel his determination to keep her from going to the Demon Realm, no matter what.
“Hey, don't scare me. You're just acting up again, aren't you?”
She had been taken in by the ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ more than once or twice.
She didn't know what the Black Flame Dragon was talking about, but this was Kim Dokja, who had predicted even <Olympus>'s invasion of the Korean Peninsula. Perhaps he knew about this situation, too.
Even if something was coming······.
Then, amid faint sparks, Han Sooyoung's hand traced the air like a brush.
―The 73rd Demon Realm will be destroyed.
The first to notice it was the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint.
Reclining atop the industrial complex's battlements, she let the pipe fall from her mouth.
“······That fellow was right.”
With her quiet murmur, the Breaking the Sky Divine Sword (破天神劍) slid from behind her back, radiating dazzling light.
Since earning the name Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, she had wielded this sword in earnest fewer than ten times.
The sword that had earned her the name of Murim's calamity.
Feeling the sword settle into her palm, the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint suddenly found it absurd.
Calamity (災害).
What could be called a calamity?
To humans, a calamity meant no more than a natural phenomenon on a local scale. A landslide, a tidal wave, an earthquake. An immense phenomenon that human strength could not even resist.
But to transcendents, these were merely physical phenomena they could manipulate.
Beings who far surpassed the limits of humanity. Those who could cause landslides and tidal waves with a single stroke of a blade—or quell them instead.
And so, to transcendents like the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, the word calamity had to mean something wholly different from what it meant to ordinary humans.
Perhaps the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint was now facing the answer.
Bzzzzzzzt!
A tiny spark flashed, and Kyrgios was already beside her.

The aura of [Electrification] was already billowing from Kyrgios's body. The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint slowly drew up her magic power as well. The two transcendents gazed together at the farthest reaches of the sky. Kyrgios asked,
“Is it that thing after all?”
Something approaching from there with an unmistakable presence, though not yet visible to the naked eye. The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint answered gravely.
“There's no doubt. It's the one that tried to swallow the <First Murim>.”
The atmosphere turning pitch-black.
From the far side of the universe that swallowed even light, something was approaching, devouring the disrupted probability.
[Hidden Scenario ― ‘Escape the Demon Realm’ is beginning!]
At that moment, every dokkaebi in the Bureau was focused on the panel screen.
“Are you kidding me? A scenario's appeared, so why isn't there a single dokkaebi to run it?”
The other dokkaebis in the Bureau held Bihyung back as he raged alone. After the ‘Demon King Selection’ ended, every dokkaebi operating a channel had withdrawn from the 73rd Demon Realm.
“Where's Baram-nim? And you, Dokgak, you fucking bastard!”
“You were going crazy trying to swallow up the Demon Realm channels, so why the hell are you here? If this is how it's going to be, let me go!”
“Bihyung, do you think it's possible to broadcast from there right now?”
Even the proud Dokgak had given up on running this scenario.
There was good reason: the Bureau had expended more probability than permitted during the ‘Demon King Selection’. Of course, that was not the only problem.
―Baat!
The cry of a baby dokkaebi who knew nothing.
Some dokkaebis sighed and turned away, while others stared at the screen as though determined to watch until the very end.
An unfathomable being that had crossed the universe of the <Star Stream> was covering the sky of the 73rd Demon Realm.
Rrrrrrrumble!
Not every being lives as a parasite on ‘scenarios’.

If constellations subsist on orderly ‘stories’, Outer Gods base their existence on chaotic ‘stories’. Beings born from the unconscious of stories. Monsters roaming the deep sea (深海) of scenarios unnamed by dokkaebis.
‘That isn't a proper scenario.’
Watching ‘it’ open its enormous mouth, Bihyung clenched his fists in despair.
‘Run, Kim Dokja.’
“······What's this?”
It was several minutes later that Jung Heewon noticed ‘it’.
Every hair on her body suddenly stood on end, and cold sweat ran down her spine.
Looking around, she saw citizens collapsing to the ground, losing consciousness or vomiting blood. Beside her, Lee Jihye was clawing at her own shoulder with glazed eyes.
“Jihye! Snap out of it!”
Only after Heewon shook her shoulders several times did Lee Jihye manage to come to her senses and lift her head.
“Ugh, aah, uh······ Unnie······.”
Her nails had already dug into her shoulder, drawing blood.
Jung Heewon turned toward the square. Yoo Sangah was already moving.
“Everyone, gather over here!”
At the sound of her voice, imbued with magic power, the companions began coming to their senses one by one.
“Wh-what is that?”
Lee Hyunsung and the children looked up at the sky. Lee Gilyoung staggered and sank to the ground, while Shin Yoosung clung to Lee Hyunsung, trembling all over.
At that moment, every companion in the square was thinking the same thing.
It didn't matter how many books they had read or how many words they knew.
‘It's indescribable.’
Yoo Sangah, Lee Hyunsung, Jung Heewon. All the words humanity possessed were powerless before the approaching being.
A pitch-black ‘something’ that had covered the entire sky.
The companions could not understand what they were looking at in the slightest. And so they had lost all means of responding.
When a typhoon blows, you can paste newspaper over the windows. When a tidal wave comes, you can enter a sturdy high-rise. When fallout begins, you can hide in a basement with thick protective walls.
But that.
What on earth could stop that?
Could it even be stopped?
Bzzzzzzz······.
It was then that a man appeared in the lightless sky.
A being shining brilliantly as he expended probability.
A trace of relief crossed Jung Heewon's face when she saw him.
Most of the constellations who had attended the banquet had left the Demon Realm two days earlier.
But not all of them.
Amid dazzling sparks, the man stepped onto the battlements.
[Hah (喝)! Everyone, come to your senses!]
Cheok Jungyeong, Goryeo’s First Sword.
As his mighty lion's roar rang along the entire wall, a few strong-minded incarnations seemed to barely regain their senses. They were looking at Cheok Jungyeong.
They didn't know what was approaching.
But they had Cheok Jungyeong on their side.
And Cheok Jungyeong had fought an ‘Outer God’ before.
[Outer God! Why have you come here? This is not your scenario!]
His lion's roar rang out toward the sky. At the waves of energy in his voice, hope began to light the incarnations' faces, one by one. Cheok Jungyeong shouted again.
[You are a great Outer God, yet all you do is gobble up surplus probability!]
But despite his repeated cries, the sky gave no answer.
As an elephant fails to notice an ant, ‘it’ did not so much as glance at Cheok Jungyeong.
Cheok Jungyeong's expression hardened.
If an elephant couldn't see an ant, he would make it see.
[■■■■■! ‘The Indescribable Distance’!]
At that instant, something looked at Cheok Jungyeong.
Bzzzzzzzzzt! Boom!

Sparks exploded all over Cheok Jungyeong's body. His skin was scorched black. His powerful muscles ruptured and bled, and Star Relics shattered by the sparks turned to ash and drifted through the air. That was the price of merely calling its name. Even so, Cheok Jungyeong did not retreat. He drew his sword.
[······This sword has cut through mountains, through seas, and even through the sun. This time, I will use it to cut through you.]
A vastness that could not be bound together as ‘one’ filled Cheok Jungyeong's vision.

A hopeless immensity in which he could not tell where to cut, where it began, or where it ended. Within that distance, so infinite that not even the slightest possibility existed, Cheok Jungyeong moved.
[Ooooooooooh!]
Shooting forth like a ray of light, Cheok Jungyeong pierced the heavens.
With the first strike, a thousand men.
With the second, a mighty mountain.
A sword that cleaved the sea with the third.
That sword shone like a meteor shower as it slashed down through the vast darkness.
For the briefest moment, a thread of light was drawn across the abyss in the sky.
The incarnations shuddered at the sight of that light.
Goryeo's greatest warrior was fighting an Outer God.
The next instant, a strange sound came from the sky. It was like a star fading at the end of its life in a distant galaxy.
And something fell from the sky.
Someone with sharp eyesight spotted it first.

Arms severed, legs burst open. An incarnation body with only half its torso remaining was plummeting toward the ground. Horror and disbelief. Even those who could not see Cheok Jungyeong's expression could tell what he felt.
A sword that had cleaved mighty mountains and seas, and even cut through the sun.
There were things even such a sword could not cut.
From the very beginning, it had been ‘something that could not be cut’.
Bzzzzzzz······.
It was the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint who caught Cheok Jungyeong's incarnation body.
[······Remember the sword mark.]
With those parting words, Cheok Jungyeong's incarnation body vanished.
It had been the incarnation body of a Narrative-grade constellation, no less.
He was the one who had broken Surya's train and severed an Outer God's leg.
Yet a constellation like that had been incapacitated and lost his incarnation body in a single instant of combat.
“U-uwaaaaaaah!”
The citizens' screams rose amid the terror consuming their minds.
Darkness that filled the horizon in every direction.
The ground writhed, something stirring like a child in the womb.
Scritch, scritch, scritch, scritch······.
A sound like an enormous insect devouring enormous prey.
In the distance, the horizon could be seen creeping closer.
The light illuminating the ground grew steadily fainter.
[The ‘73rd Demon Realm’ groans in pain!]
The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint and Kyrgios had already seen this sight once in the <First Murim>.
Kyrgios spoke.
“······Thanks to my crazy disciple, I might just die here.”
“It seems neither of us has any luck with disciples.”
The world's screams rang out. Darkness filled with nothing but greed was approaching, devouring everything in the 73rd Demon Realm.
Grinding his teeth, Kyrgios concentrated all the magic power of White Pure Star Energy.
“······This is why we have to respect ‘probability’.”
‘The Indescribable Distance’.
This god, called the calamity of the stars, was in a sense the very backlash of probability itself.
A cleaner born of chaos, setting right the laws of the <Star Stream> that had gone awry.
“They've already gone awry. Nothing we can do about that. I'll twist them to the worst possible extreme, with everything I have!”
At the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's cry, the Status of the two transcendents blazed brilliantly.
The sky-breaking sword that shattered the heavens.
The supreme technique of the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, Murim's god, shot toward the sky with the power of the <First Murim> held within it.
Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship (破天劍道).
Ultimate Technique (絶技).
Breaking the Sky Meteor Art (破天流星決).
The very sword technique Yoo Joonghyuk had once used.
The supreme technique of Breaking the Sky Swordsmanship that had struck down and cut through countless constellations.
Krrrrrrash!

The ferocious strokes of the sky-breaking sword burst forth across the heavens. An explosive deluge of magic power embroidered the air with brilliant light, and the meteor-like sword strokes spread through it in splendid patterns.
Yet ‘it’ did not suffer so much as a scratch.
Sword strikes vanishing into emptiness, like dust drifting through the universe.
Even her sword that could shatter the sky could not shatter the universe.
“Kyrgios!”
At the signal, Kyrgios leaped from the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's shoulder.
Bzzzzzzzt!

Trailing dazzling light, Kyrgios accelerated with the power of [Electrification], piercing the atmosphere and soaring through the heavens. A universe with no end in sight. Within that fathomless darkness, Kyrgios sensed the darkness covering the sky, and beyond it, the gazes of the stars watching him.
[The constellation ‘Prisoner of the Golden Headband’ emits golden light from his eyes.]
[The constellation ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ roars!]
That was where the stars dwelled.
A place the short arms of a human could never reach.
Kyrgios knew that, too.
Crack!
So he had striven.
Striven, and striven again.
Crack! Crack!

Stepping on fragments of the Meteor Art left by the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint, Kyrgios leaped higher, ever higher. As though racing toward an unreachable star, the mortal who had built his history through years of painstaking effort finally reached the seats (座) of the dazzling stars.
The universe he had reached at last.
Kyrgios had finally reached a place from which he could see ‘it’.
Something reminiscent of a vast mist.
The mist, lacking any definite shape, was greedily devouring the planet called the ‘73rd Demon Realm’.
At the center of that mist was the threadlike sword mark Cheok Jungyeong had left.
White-blue power, compressed to its utmost limit, gathered in Kyrgios's right hand.
[In the beginning, the universe arose from the smallest thing.]
With a fierce shout, Kyrgios thrust out his right hand.
Like the eruption of the Big Bang, the white-blue energy drove into the heart of the mist.
Boooooooom!
Every citizen shut their eyes as a flash turned the sky white.
For an instant, the power of the two transcendents overwhelmed the universe and covered the darkness of the world.
Then, when the light abruptly went out, a vast fissure had appeared in the darkness covering the sky. The citizens shouted.
“Th-they did it.”
“They did it! The transcendents did it!”
Bzzzzzzzz······.
But the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's expression was grim.
Watching Kyrgios hurtling back through the sky, she smiled faintly.
“This is as far as we go.”
Rrrrrrrumble.
Beyond the falling Kyrgios, the sky was splitting apart.
Something was waking in the pitch-black darkness.
It was an eye.

An enormous eye that looked down on the world in contempt. Within its snow-white lens, a pitch-black pupil followed Kyrgios's back as he fell. The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint gasped, and Kyrgios turned.
The transcendents' magic power collided with an irresistible Status.
Ssssssss······.

Kyrgios's tightly bound long hair was turning white. The Breaking the Sky Sword Saint's muscles, swollen as though about to burst, were wasting away. As though aging, the bodies of the two transcendents were dying before the unfathomable span of time.
The universe's ‘Status’ was on another level.
They had surpassed mortals to become transcendents and gained the power to humble even constellations.
But their history of grueling training was not even a speck of dust compared with the ‘history’ of that cosmic being.
[‘The Indescribable Distance’ looks at the ‘73rd Demon Realm’.]
Citizens driven mad ran wild.
“Escape! Escape!”
“Waaaaaaaagh!”
Not even knowing what they were saying, the citizens let out cries like wild beasts.
[Portals cannot be used due to the intervention of a powerful being.]
“What, wh-what······.”
“Whatwhatwhatwhatwhat······.”
“Wak wak wak wak wak wak wak······.”
The citizens' bodies swelled with lumps and burst apart. Some transformed into grotesque beings; others vomited tentacles from their mouths.
The world was going mad.
But not everyone. Even beneath the gaze of that impossible being, some still refused to let go of their blades.
“······Not yet. We can still fight.”
It was Jung Heewon. Gasping for breath and fighting down her nausea, she refused to kneel. Her companions gathered one by one and stood beside her.
The reason they could endure was simple.
[The Giant Story ‘Demon Realm's Spring’ protects the incarnations.]
Because this world was refusing to be destroyed.
Because they were the very history of this ‘73rd Demon Realm’.
Rrrrrrrumble!
[The constellation ‘Queen of the Darkest Spring’ shouts at you to flee!]
[The constellation ‘Abandoned Lover of the Labyrinth’ screams.]
[The constellation ‘Seo Ae Il Pil’ closes his eyes in pain.]
The companions knew it, too.
Any power they possessed was paltry before that mighty being.
Clutching the Sword of Judgment, Jung Heewon vomited blood and cried out.
“Uriel! Please!”
The ‘Demon-like Judge of Fire’ gave no response.
Neither Gong Pildu's ‘Defense Master’ nor Lee Hyunsung's ‘Master of Steel’.
This time, they did not answer their incarnations' requests.
No, they could not answer.
[All the stars in the night sky fall silent.]
The constellations in that sky voiced no condemnation.
Just as thunder, lightning, and storms could not be condemned, ‘that thing’ had never been something subject to condemnation.
Rrrrrumble.
Terrified, Osu wet himself.
Jang Hayoung sank to the ground, retching.
A stunned Gong Pildu began raising meaningless walls. Trembling, Han Myungoh searched desperately for somewhere to plant his single foot. But his foot would not move.
Crrrrrrrack!
Before that world-devouring being, there was no ground on which to set his foot.
“Dokja-ssi!”
And there was Kim Dokja.
At Yoo Sangah's cry, everyone looked up at the same place.
The top of the unfinished clock tower. Kim Dokja stood at the edge of slowly flowing time.
[The constellation ‘Demon King of Salvation’ gazes at the night sky.]
The only star illuminating the lightless night sky.
There stood the ‘Demon King of Salvation’.
Jung Heewon murmured.
“······Dokja-ssi?”
Beyond the rays of light Kim Dokja emitted, an enormous eye was looking down at the world.
The moment she met its gaze, Jung Heewon trembled with the feeling that she would go mad.
Rrrrrrrumble!
The earth buckled as seismic waves sent the ground surging toward them like a tidal wave.
[The ‘73rd Demon Realm’ howls in pain!]
The shattered crust spewed lava, and the overflowing heat vanished once more into the belly of the void.
The whole world was closing in around the [Industrial Complex].
If things were this bad here, it was obvious what must have happened to the other [Industrial Complexes].
Bzzzzzzt!
The transcendents' magic power, amplified by Stories, stirred.
They could not directly oppose that ‘eye’, but they could slow the seismic waves.
“Hurry up, you foolish disciple!”
At Kyrgios's cry, space distorted beyond the industrial complex's battlements. The horizon, eaten away by the immense mist, was disappearing into black nothingness.
No, it was no longer a horizon.
Even so, Jung Heewon did not let go of her thread of hope.
If she had heard correctly, the masters and Kim Dokja had already foreseen this situation.
“Ajusshi! What the hell is going on?”
Cheok Jungyeong's incarnation body had vanished, and Kyrgios and the Breaking the Sky Sword Saint had been reduced to that state.
But there was no way that ‘Kim Dokja’ would have done nothing while things deteriorated this far.
Kim Dokja's lips, ceaselessly murmuring something into the air. His eyes, moving busily as though searching for something in that distant universe.
Jung Heewon realized.
Just as they had not given up, neither had Kim Dokja.
Kim Dokja slowly descended toward the ground.
Taking that as her signal, Jung Heewon shouted.
“Everyone, get ready!”
Having activated [Steel Transformation], Lee Hyunsung asked,
“Dokja-ssi! What should we do?”
Everyone was looking at Kim Dokja.
They didn't know how.
But Kim Dokja would have something in mind.
